title: The Brahmabindu Upanishad
attributionNote: One of the Atharvana (minor) Upanishads, transmitted without an author's name. GRETIL's e-text follows Ramamaya Tarkaratna's edition of the Atharvana-Upanishads, Calcutta 1872 (Bibliotheca Indica 76), and was input by Oliver Hellwig.
description: The Brahmabindu Upaniṣad is a short teaching on the mind as the cause of both bondage and release: mind alone is the cause of men's bondage and liberation — bound when it is attached to objects, released when it is without them. It distinguishes the impure from the pure mind, describes the practice by which the mind is brought to rest and the sound of the inner ātman heard, and closes with the knower who neither comes nor goes.
historicalContext: The text stands with the other Atharvana Upanishads on yoga and liberation — the Nādabindu, the Amṛtabindu, the Dhyānabindu — which the yoga and Vedanta traditions read as the scriptural form of their practice; the Brahmabindu is quoted for its teaching that purification of the mind is the whole of yoga.
availabilityNote: Complete: the 22 verses are streamed from GRETIL at read time and indexed in reading order, because the Upanishad is a single continuous text without the divisions a chapter reference would name.
